$comment: EP-PHASE-DEADLINE (WF3, 2026-09-15) — THE R-X DISPOSITION REGISTRY FOR THE
`execution.*` DURATION DECLARATIONS (Spec 124 §5 R-X).
Spec 124 R-X: 'a frozen declaration that has no live executor is a declaration,
not a deletion — it must carry a disposition row, never silently drift.' R-X's
own text names the generalization this file builds: its existing registry
(`write-class-disposition.json`) covers ONLY `outputs.write_discipline.class`
and `sharing.on_contention`, and extending it to the other `execution.*`
postures was recorded there as 'not yet built'.
The founding measurement (cloud run 34971921528 / 34971921328, main@824ef357,
2026-09-15): `enrich_parcels` declares `budget:150m`, `txn_budget:130m` and
`step_timeout:180m`. A repo-wide grep found ZERO executors for any of the three
— `grep -rn 'txn_budget|\.budget' scripts/lib/` returns nothing at all, and the
only `step_timeout` consumer (`run-chain.js`, `Number(scriptEntry.
step_timeout_minutes || 0)`) reads `scripts/manifest.json`, NOT the descriptor.
The declarations read as enforcement to every reader and enforce nothing. The
run that exposed this died at the GitHub Actions 300-min wall clock, the ONLY
live element of the whole declared ladder.
CLOSED MENU — a row's `disposition` is exactly one of:
* `executed`    — a named, live executor consumes the declaration. The row
MUST cite `executor.file` + `executor.anchor`, and the lock
greps the anchor out of the file rather than trusting this
registry's own prose.
* `descriptive` — documentation only: the value is declared, is NOT enforced,
and SAYS SO. A `descriptive` row MUST be named in Spec 124's
own R-X disposition table, so a reader of the spec (not just
of this file) learns the declaration is inert.
There is no third value. An invented one is RED.
Both directions are locked by src/tests/execution-budget-disposition.infra.test.ts:
(1) every `execution.*` duration key any LIVE descriptor declares has a row
here, and no row here is an orphan;
(2) every `executed` row's cited executor anchor resolves in its cited file;
(3) `step_timeout`'s own wiring is drift-locked BOTH ways: for every slug in
`wired[]`, the descriptor's declared duration and `manifest.scripts[slug].
step_timeout_minutes` must agree in minutes; every other converted step
declaring `step_timeout` must appear in `pending[]`, so the ten steps whose
declaration is still inert are a DECLARED, dated gap rather than an
invisible one;
(4) every `descriptive` row is named in Spec 124's R-X disposition table;
(5) `enrich_parcels`' stop-mechanism LADDER holds (Spec 118 §3): the CI wall
clock > the manifest step ceiling > the per-phase deadline. A ladder whose
rungs invert is the defect this WF3 closed, re-armed.

executor.role: the post-check ceiling fallback for a step that declares no step_post_check_statement_timeout_minutes tunable; also read per-entry by scripts/lib/step/plausibility.js

statement_timeout.why: Already live before this WF3 — listed here so the registry covers the WHOLE duration family and an orphan/missing-row check is meaningful in both directions.

executor.role: Spec 118 §3 layer 3 — run-chain arms a per-step SIGTERM ceiling from manifest.scripts[slug].step_timeout_minutes; absent/0 is INERT (run-chain.js's own docblock). The descriptor's execution.step_timeout is the DECLARATION; the manifest key is the EXECUTION, and (3) below is what keeps the two from drifting apart.

step_timeout.pending_why: Measured 2026-09-15: 12 converted descriptors declare execution.step_timeout; only refresh_snapshot had the manifest counterpart that executes it. enrich_parcels is wired by this WF3 because it is the step whose declaration was measured inert against a real 300-min kill. The remaining ten are a DECLARED gap, not a silent one — filed in docs/reports/review_followups.md; wiring them is its own WF2 (each ceiling needs its own measured duration, and a ceiling set below a step's real runtime turns a healthy run into a failure). UPDATED 2026-09-16 (batch-2 Phase 0.9 I5): geocode_permits joins the list at the folded commit 5 — its descriptor declares execution.step_timeout "15m" and manifest.scripts.geocode_permits carries no step_timeout_minutes (measured), so the declaration is INERT exactly like the other eleven. Not wired here on purpose: a ceiling needs its OWN measured duration, and one set below a step's real runtime converts a healthy run into a failure. This step's honest number is not yet known — its 65 recorded runs predate per-step duration capture on this branch — so it is DECLARED pending rather than guessed. UPDATED 2026-09-18 (batch2 P1.1): assert_parcel_sanity joins the list — its descriptor declares execution.step_timeout "45m" (§8's own honestly-UNMEASURED prediction, per R-AQ: a ceiling measures the step, an instance measures the hardware, and the first real cloud measurement replaces this number rather than the ceiling being raised to absorb it) and manifest.scripts.assert_parcel_sanity carries no step_timeout_minutes — the same declared-not-wired gap as the other twelve, not wired here for the identical reason (no cloud run has measured this step's real duration yet).

budget.why: No executor exists anywhere in scripts/ (grep -rn '\.budget' scripts/lib/ => zero hits, 2026-09-15). It documents the step's INTENDED wall-clock envelope for a human sizing a CI ceiling; nothing measures a run against it and nothing aborts on it. Kept (not removed) per R-X: a declaration with a disposition is legible; a deleted field is a silent loss of the sizing intent. The ENFORCED ceiling for a step is manifest.scripts[slug].step_timeout_minutes (see step_timeout above) — budget is the number an operator reads when choosing that one.

txn_budget.why: No executor exists anywhere in scripts/ (grep -rn 'txn_budget' scripts/lib/ => zero hits, 2026-09-15). It documents how much of `budget` the step's own transaction is expected to hold open — the number that matters for vacuum-horizon reasoning (enrich_parcels' EP-D17 maintenance ruling is exactly this arithmetic done by hand). Enforcing it would require a transaction-scoped deadline distinct from the per-phase one EP-PHASE-DEADLINE built; that is a separate WF and is filed, not smuggled in here.

ladder.$why: Spec 118 §3's stop-mechanism hierarchy for enrich_parcels, after EP-PHASE-DEADLINE. Each rung must be strictly tighter than the one outside it, or the outer rung is the only one that can ever fire — which is precisely the 2026-09-15 incident (the GH wall clock was the entire enforcement stack).
